$comment: LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT for the op engine. Each case is an op log applied to empty_project_doc(unitsDisplay); expectedStateHash is stateHash(ProjectDoc) = sha256(canonicalJson(doc)) as 64 lowercase hex chars. BOTH packages/model/src/fold.test.ts AND apps/api/garh_model/tests/test_fold.py must read THIS file and assert every row. A mismatch means the two implementations disagree about what a design IS — never paste the new hash to make it pass; find out which side moved. Generated by fixtures/model/_tools/generate_golden_states.py.
notes: Ops are the wire form: {type, payload} with camelCase payload keys, integer mm only.
An absent payload key means 'unchanged'; an explicit null means 'clear it'.
Element arrays are sorted by id before hashing; storeys keep their semantic order.
Room and slab ids are DERIVED, so they are part of the hash: they pin derived_id().

cases.name: empty-document
cases.description: The initial state every op log folds from: empty_project_doc('ft-in') with no ops applied. Pins the defaults (plinth 600, sill 900, lintel 2100, parapet 1000) and the exact key set of the document.

cases.name: plot-only
cases.description: Plot ops 1-4 with no building: 30x40ft boundary, north 0, a 9m road on edge 0, and the Bengaluru rule pack. plot.set_reg_profile also writes meta.regProfileRef.

cases.name: brief-merge-patch
cases.description: RFC 7386 merge patch semantics: nested objects merge, an explicit null DELETES a key, a later scalar replaces. Ends with data = {bedrooms: 4, budget: {totalInr: 9500000}, style: 'contemporary'} — 'baths' was deleted by the null.

cases.name: two-room-plan
cases.description: The canonical fixture: 6000x4000 ground floor, 230mm external walls, a 115mm spine at x=3000. Room detection must find EXACTLY two rooms of 10_661_560 mm2 each ((2943-115)x(3885-115)), with derived ids, plus one derived floor slab grown outward to (-115,-115)..(6115,4115).

cases.name: two-room-plan-with-openings
cases.description: The two-room plan plus a 900x2100 door at offset 1500 on the south wall and a 1200x1200 window at offset 2000 (sill 900) on the west wall. Openings never change room polygons.

cases.name: rooms-assigned
cases.description: room.assign / room.set_target on the two derived rooms. The room ids here are DERIVED (sha256 of storeyId|polygonKey -> 26 Crockford chars), so this case also pins derived_id() and polygon_key() across languages.

cases.name: wall-split-and-move
cases.description: wall.split at 3000mm re-hosts the openings BEYOND the split onto the new wall with a rebased offset (the 4500mm door becomes 1500mm on wall WS2) and leaves the 1500mm door where it is; wall.move then shifts the spine to x=3500, which re-cuts both rooms while PRESERVING their ids (max-Jaccard match).

cases.name: storeys-stair-levels
cases.description: G+1 with a dogleg stair on the ground floor: 18 risers x 167mm = 3006mm against a 3000mm storey (inside the +/-10mm tolerance). The first floor slab must carry the stair footprint as a cut-out, and levels.set with an explicit plinth re-derives fflPerStoreyMm = [750, 3750].

cases.name: furnishings-and-facade
cases.description: The non-geometric families in one log: a column (default 230x230 applied by fold), furniture, a balcony (defaults for railing/projection/slab), a facade kit with two components, a merge patch on one component's params, a material assignment and a sheet annotation. Pins every 'defaults applied by fold' path.

cases.name: solver-apply-option
cases.description: solver.apply_option carries its own expansion and folds as ONE atomic group, so this log must produce exactly the same document (and hash) as applying the four inner ops directly — asserted by the test, not just by this hash.

cases.name: unicode-and-escapes
cases.description: Canonical-JSON string rules: non-ASCII is emitted literally as UTF-8 (never \uXXXX), while backslash, quote, tab, newline and other C0 controls are escaped minimally with LOWERCASE hex. Devanagari, an em dash and a rupee sign all appear in real Indian briefs.

cases.name: transform-paste-floor-up
cases.description: The op log a PASTE dispatches: five walls and their two openings copied onto a new first floor with a zero delta. No new op type — wall.add and opening.add, with ids derived from the gesture's group id so the log is reproducible. Applied as one group, this is one undo.

cases.name: transform-mirror-copy
cases.description: The op log a MIRROR (keep original) dispatches: the same five walls reflected about x = 9000 onto clear ground. Every 'in-*' swing becomes 'out-*' with the hinge token unchanged and offsetMm untouched — a reflection is an isometry along the wall and orientation-reversing across it.

cases.name: transform-mirror-in-place
cases.description: The op log a MIRROR with 'keep original' OFF dispatches — flipping the plan. It deletes every selected wall before re-adding any of them, at the ORIGINAL ids, because south and north swap positions and wall.move would trip WALL_DUPLICATE whichever went first. The openings the delete cascade took come back with the hand flipped.
